doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: First records with Tony Scott and the Minton's gig
summary: Katz's first records with Tony Scott and about six months at Minton's with Philly Joe Jones and Milt Hinton.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yup. And they’re good records. The first one was done — not the very first one, the first one was at an Army camp in New Jersey with Milt and I forget who the drummer was, and Tony. We played jobs all over. But when you got this Minton’s gig, it was about now, the early part of 1953, we were there about six months almost, it was really a fantastic gig, and the group got really tight. It was with Philly Joe and Milt and this was before — just between the time Milt went in, was with Cab Calloway and the time that he went in to studios and became this incredible all things to all men person.
